prompt: This person values the process of verifying information.
options: I use an AI tool to generate alternative explanations after I have tried the textbook. It is useful when one description does not make sense, but I never copy its answer directly. I compare the explanation with lecture slides and write a note in my own words. The checking takes time, yet that process is part of the learning.

The greatest benefit is language support. I draft my argument first, then ask the tool to identify sentences that are unclear. I reject many of its suggestions because they sound too formal or change my meaning. Universities should teach students how to evaluate advice rather than simply banning the technology.

I experimented with automatic summaries, but they encouraged me to skip difficult sections of articles. My notes became shorter while my understanding became weaker. I now use the tool only at the end, to test whether my own summary has missed a major point. It should follow reading, not replace it.

Group study has become more productive because we use a tool to create possible quiz questions before meetings. Each member checks a different set, and we discuss the ones that are ambiguous. The useful part is not the generated question itself; it is the disagreement that forces us to justify an interpretation.
